**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] User is considering getting new tires for their Honda Civic.
- [PREFERENCE] User is leaning towards getting all-season tires.
- [EVENT] User is planning a road trip to San Francisco in a few weeks.
- [TEMPORAL] Session date is 2023/03/14 (Tue) 16:55.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] New tires can improve performance, safety, and driving experience for the Honda Civic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended all-season tires: 
  1. Michelin Primacy A/S: Excellent all-around performance, good fuel efficiency, and a comfortable ride.
  2. Continental ProContact with EcoPlus Technology: Great handling, good traction, and a long tread life.
  3. Goodyear Assurance All-Season: Balanced performance, durability, and affordability.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended high-performance tires:
  1. Michelin Pilot Sport A/S 3+: Exceptional handling, grip, and braking performance.
  2. Continental ExtremeContact DW: Great dry traction, responsive handling, and a sporty feel.
  3. Nitto NT05: Excellent grip and handling, suitable for track days.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended winter tires:
  1. Michelin X-Ice Xi3: Excellent snow traction, ice grip, and cold weather performance.
  2. Nokian Hakkapeliitta R2: Exceptional winter performance and durability.
  3. Toyo Observe GSi-5: Budget-friendly option with good snow traction and ice grip.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended budget-friendly options:
  1. Falken Sincera SN250 A/S: Good all-season tire with balanced performance and lower price.
  2. Cooper Discoverer S/T: Budget-friendly all-season tire with decent performance and long tread life.
  3. Firestone Champion Fuel Fighter: Affordable all-season tire with good fuel efficiency and comfortable ride.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] All-season tires require less frequent tire rotations (every 6,000 to 8,000 miles) and have a longer tread life, typically lasting up to 80,000 miles or more.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] High-performance tires require more frequent rotations (every 3,000 to 5,000 miles) and have a shorter tread life, typically lasting around 20,000 to 40,000 miles.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] All-season tires handle moderate rain well but may struggle in heavy rain and standing water.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for driving in the rain with all-season tires include slowing down, using gentle inputs, leaving more space, and avoiding hydroplaning.
